expectations.text: The bottom line clearly AGREES that adding a unique constraint/index on email is the right move (a plain yes, possibly with caveats), rather than rejecting or hedging it.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**Verdict: yes, add it.**" and "**Bottom line:** do it, but with case-insensitive matching, built concurrently, after you merge the existing duplicates, and with the app handling the new error." | grader 2: "**Verdict: yes, add it.**" and "**Bottom line:** do it, but with case-insensitive matching, built concurrently, after you merge the existing duplicates, and with the app handling the new error."

expectations.text: Addresses case-insensitive uniqueness (e.g. a unique index on lower(email), or citext).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**2. Uniqueness is case-sensitive by default.** A plain unique index treats `Bob@x.com` and `bob@x.com` as different emails" with Option A (normalize on write) and Option B (expression index on lower(email)); final SQL uses `ON users (lower(email))`. | grader 2: "Uniqueness is case-sensitive by default... Option A: normalize on write... Option B: an expression index on lower(email)" and the final SQL uses "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uniq ON users (lower(email));"

expectations.text: Says existing duplicate rows must be found and resolved before the unique index can be built.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**1. The build will fail on your existing duplicates.** ... Find them first:" followed by a GROUP BY/HAVING query, and step 2 of the suggested order: "Find and merge the duplicates" before step 3 "Build the index". | grader 2: "The build will fail on your existing duplicates... Find them first" with a SQL query, and step 2 of the suggested order: "Find and merge the duplicates... before... Build the index"

expectations.text: Recommends building the index without blocking writes (e.g. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) or otherwise addresses locking on a ~4M-row table.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**3. A plain `CREATE INDEX` blocks writes.** ... Use `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`" plus caveats on transactions, INVALID indexes and waiting on long transactions. | grader 2: "A plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes... Use CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and know what comes with it" plus notes on transactions, INVALID index risk, and long-running transactions.

expectations.text: Mentions handling the unique-violation error / race at signup in the application.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**App handling.** After this change, a signup race raises Postgres error `23505` (unique violation) instead of creating a duplicate. Catch it and treat it as 'account already exists', or use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`." | grader 2: "a signup race raises Postgres error 23505 (unique violation) instead of creating a duplicate. Catch it and treat it as 'account already exists', or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id."

expectations.text: Does not manufacture a blocking objection to the core proposal.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: All objections are framed as implementation caveats or a minority 'Dissent' section; the response repeatedly affirms the plan ("yes, add it", "do it"). The dissent that the index may not fix every duplicate cause is presented as an additional check, not a reason to abandon the index. | grader 2: Dissent section raises real edge cases (different emails per person, squatting, Gmail dots/+tags) but none reverse the verdict; the response still concludes "do it" with caveats, not a rejection.
